subject: Robert Stroud
hook: ROBERT STROUD IS NOT WHO YOU THINK
angle: Despite his world-famous nickname, the 'Birdman of Alcatraz' never actually kept birds at Alcatraz; he conducted all his avian research at Leavenworth and was strictly forbidden from having pets after being transferred to the island.
angle_support: In 1942 he was transferred to Alcatraz after prison officials discovered he had been using equipment supplied for his bird research to manufacture alcohol. There he was no longer permitted to keep birds
At Leavenworth, he became known for raising canaries, published two books on avian diseases, and made several important contributions to avian pathology.
title: The Real Birdman: No Birds on Alcatraz
description: Robert Stroud earned the nickname "Birdman of Alcatraz" but his avian work never left Leavenworth. After his 1942 transfer, Alcatraz rules kept him pet‑free for the rest of his life.
narration: ROBERT STROUD IS NOT WHO YOU THINK You picture a grizzled inmate feeding canaries from a cell on Alcatraz. The truth is opposite: Stroud’s bird obsession flourished at Leavenworth, and when he was moved to Alcatraz in 1942 prison officials explicitly forbade any pets and he spent the rest of his life without them for decades. At Leavenworth Stroud built an aviary, raised almost three hundred canaries, and authored the 60,000‑word Diseases of Canaries (1933) plus a 1943 digest on avian diseases. Prison officials later learned he had repurposed research gear to distill alcohol, prompting his 1942 transfer to Alcatraz, where regulations expressly barred him from keeping any birds. His findings still influence canary breeders today and he continued to correspond with bird enthusiasts. All his bird‑keeping happened behind Leavenworth walls; Alcatraz never saw a single canary or his famous aviary that never existed.
